title: While Loops
summary: `while condition do ... end` repeats a block as long as the condition is true. Check happens before each iteration — zero iterations if the condition starts false.

syntax:
while condition do
    -- runs while condition is truthy
end

details.heading: Yielding inside
details.body: If the body calls something that yields (like `task.wait()`), the loop pauses there and resumes later. A while loop with no wait and an always-true condition locks up its thread.

explanation.whatItIs: A loop that keeps repeating while a condition stays true. 'While the door is closed, keep knocking.'
explanation.whyItExists: Some work is 'keep doing this until something changes' — waiting for players, ticking timers, polling state.
whenToUse: Waiting for a condition: `while not target do task.wait() ... end`
Game loops driven by state: `while roundActive do ... task.wait(1) end`
When you don't know the iteration count up front
whenNotToUse: For counting a known number of times — use a numeric `for`
For walking arrays — use `for i, v in array` / `ipairs`
Almost never without a `task.wait()`/yield somewhere in the body
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
while condition do
    body
end

-- is exactly:
if condition then
    body
    if condition then
        body
        ...     -- repeats until condition is false/nil
    end
end
```
tips: In Roblox, always include `task.wait()` in loops that run over time — it yields to the engine and prevents freezing
Prefer RunService.Heartbeat/Stepped connections over `while true do task.wait()` for per-frame logic
The condition is re-evaluated every iteration — changing a variable inside the loop controls when it stops
commonMistakes: `while true do` with no wait = infinite loop that hangs the script thread
Condition checks a stale variable that never changes inside the loop
Expecting the body to run at least once — if the condition is false at the start, it never runs (use repeat-until for that)

examples.title: Waiting for something to exist
examples.code:
-- Poll until the part appears (see also: WaitForChild)
local part
while not part do
    part = workspace:FindFirstChild("TreasureChest")
    task.wait(0.2)
end
print("Found it:", part.Name)

examples.title: A round timer
examples.code:
local timeLeft = 30
local roundActive = true

while roundActive and timeLeft > 0 do
    print(`Time left: {timeLeft}`)
    timeLeft -= 1
    task.wait(1)
end

print(if timeLeft <= 0 then "Round over!" else "Round ended early")
